question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{2d} - 1.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{2d} - 1,$ and simplify: \begin{align} \dfrac{d + 1}{\sqrt{2d} + 1} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{d+1}{\sqrt{2d} + 1} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{2d} - 1}{\sqrt{2d} - 1} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac {(d+1)(\sqrt{2d} - 1)}{(\sqrt{2d} + 1)(\sqrt{2d} - 1)} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{(d+1)(\sqrt{2d} - 1)}{(\sqrt{2d})^2 - 1^2} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{(d+1)(\sqrt{2d} - 1)}{2d - 1} & \end{align}

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{m}-m.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{m}-m,$ and simplify:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \dfrac{m}{\sqrt{m}+m}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{m}{\sqrt{m}+m}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{m}-m}{\sqrt{m}-m}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{m(\sqrt{m}-m)}{(\sqrt{m}+m)(\sqrt{m}-m)}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{m(\sqrt{m}-m)}{(\sqrt{m})^2-m^2}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{m(\sqrt{m}-m)}{m-m^2}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{\cancel{m}(\sqrt{m}-m)}{\cancel{m}(1-m)}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{m}-m}{1-m} \end{align*}

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{a} +2.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{a} +2,$ and simplify: \[ \eqalign{ \dfrac {1} {\sqrt{a} -2} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac {1} {\sqrt{a} -2} \cdot \dfrac {\sqrt{a} +2}{\sqrt{a} +2} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac {\sqrt{a} +2} {(\sqrt{a} -2)(\sqrt{a} +2)} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac {\sqrt{a} +2} {(\sqrt a)^2-2^2} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac {\sqrt{a} +2} {a-4} } \]

First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{w}-1.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{w}-1,$ and simplify:

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{w}+1}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{w}+1}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{w}-1}{\sqrt{w}-1}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{w}-1}{(\sqrt{w}+1)(\sqrt{w}-1)}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{w}-1}{(\sqrt{w})^2-1^2}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{w} - 1}{w-1} \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Rationalizing Denominators Containing a Binomial Within the Radical

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $3-\sqrt{2w+5}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $3-\sqrt{2w+5},$ and simplify:

\begin{align*} -\dfrac{4w}{3+\sqrt{2w+5}}&=\\[5pt] -\dfrac{4w}{3+\sqrt{2w+5}}\cdot \dfrac{3-\sqrt{2w+5}}{3-\sqrt{2w+5}}&=\\[5pt] -\dfrac{4w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{(3+\sqrt{2w+5})(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}&=\\[5pt] -\dfrac{4w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{3^2-(\sqrt{2w+5})^2}&=\\[5pt] -\dfrac{4w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{9-(2w+5)}&=\\[5pt] -\dfrac{4w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{4-2w}&=\\[5pt] -\dfrac{4w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{2(2-w)}&=\\[5pt] -\dfrac{2w(3-\sqrt{2w+5})}{2-w} \end{align*}

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $1 + \sqrt{1 - t}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1 + \sqrt{1 - t},$ and simplify: \begin{align} \require{cancel} \dfrac{3t}{1 - \sqrt{1 - t}} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{3t}{1 - \sqrt{1 - t}} \cdot \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{1 - t}}{1 + \sqrt{1 - t}} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{3t(1 + \sqrt{1 - t})}{(1 - \sqrt{1 - t})(1 + \sqrt{1 - t})} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{3t(1 + \sqrt{1 - t})}{1^2 - (\sqrt{1-t})^2} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{3t(1 + \sqrt{1 - t})} {1 - (1 - t)} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{3\cancel{t}(1 + \sqrt{1 - t})}{\cancel{t}} & = \\[5pt] 3(1 + \sqrt{1 - t}) & \end{align}

example.title: Rationalizing Denominators Containing a Binomial Within the Radical

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{2r-1} + 1.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{2r-1} + 1,$ and simplify: \begin{align} \dfrac{4r^2}{\sqrt{2r-1} - 1} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{4r^2}{\sqrt{2r-1} - 1} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{2r-1} + 1}{\sqrt{2r-1} + 1} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{4r^2(\sqrt{2r-1} + 1)}{(\sqrt{2r-1} - 1)(\sqrt{2r-1} + 1)} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{4r^2(\sqrt{2r-1} + 1)}{(\sqrt{2r-1})^2 - 1^2} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{4r^2(\sqrt{2r-1} + 1)} {2r - 1 - 1} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{4r^2(\sqrt{2r-1} + 1)} {2r - 2} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{2r^2(\sqrt{2r-1} + 1)} {r - 1} & \end{align}

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $7-\sqrt{x-5}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $7-\sqrt{x-5},$ and simplify: \begin{align*} \dfrac{x}{7+\sqrt{x-5}}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{x}{7+\sqrt{x-5}}\cdot \dfrac{7-\sqrt{x-5}}{7-\sqrt{x-5}}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{x(7-\sqrt{x-5})}{(7+\sqrt{x-5})(7-\sqrt{x-5})}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{7x-x\sqrt{x-5}}{7^2-(\sqrt{x-5})^2}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{7x-x\sqrt{x-5}}{49-(x-5)}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{7x-x\sqrt{x-5}}{54-x} \end{align*}

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $1-\sqrt{1-2w}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1-\sqrt{1-2w},$ and simplify:

\begin{align*} \dfrac{2}{1+\sqrt{1-2w}}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{1+\sqrt{1-2w}}\cdot \dfrac{1-\sqrt{1-2w}}{1-\sqrt{1-2w}}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{2(1-\sqrt{1-2w})}{(1+\sqrt{1-2w})(1-\sqrt{1-2w})}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{2(1-\sqrt{1-2w})}{1^2-(\sqrt{1-2w})^2}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{2(1-\sqrt{1-2w})}{1-(1-2w)}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{2(1-\sqrt{1-2w})}{2w}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{1-\sqrt{1-2w}}{w} \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Rationalizing a Denominator With Two Radicals

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{w - 3}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{w - 3},$ and simplify: \begin{align} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{w} + \sqrt{w - 3}} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{w} + \sqrt{w - 3}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{w - 3}}{\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{w - 3}} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{w - 3}}{(\sqrt{w} + \sqrt{w - 3})(\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{w - 3})} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{w - 3}}{(\sqrt{w})^2 - (\sqrt{w - 3})^2} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{w - 3}}{w - (w - 3)} &=\\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{w} - \sqrt{w - 3}}{3} & \end{align}

example.title: Rationalizing a Denominator With Two Radicals

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{x-3}-\sqrt{x-2}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{x-3}-\sqrt{x-2},$ and simplify:

\[ \eqalign{ \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{x-3}+\sqrt{x-2}} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{x-3}+\sqrt{x-2}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{x-3}-\sqrt{x-2}}{\sqrt{x-3}-\sqrt{x-2}} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{3(\sqrt{x-3}-\sqrt{x-2})}{(\sqrt{x-3}+\sqrt{x-2})(\sqrt{x-3}-\sqrt{x-2})} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{3(\sqrt{x-3}-\sqrt{x-2})}{(\sqrt{x-3})^2 - (\sqrt{x-2})^2} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{3(\sqrt{x-3}-\sqrt{x-2})}{x-3 - (x-2)} &= \\[5pt] \dfrac{3(\sqrt{x-3}-\sqrt{x-2})}{-1} &= \\[5pt] 3\sqrt{x-2} - 3\sqrt{x-3} } \]

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2},$ and simplify: \begin{align*} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3w}+\sqrt{2}}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3w}+\sqrt{2}}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2}}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2})}{(\sqrt{3w}+\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2})}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2}}{(\sqrt{3w})^2-(\sqrt{2})^2}&=\\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt{3w}-\sqrt{2}}{3w-2} \end{align*}

example.title: Rationalizing a Denominator With Two Radicals

question.explanation:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{t - 2}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{t - 2},$ and simplify: \begin{align} \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{t} - \sqrt{t - 2}} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{t} - \sqrt{t - 2}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{t - 2}}{\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{t - 2}} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{4(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{t - 2})}{(\sqrt{t} - \sqrt{t - 2})(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{t - 2})} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{4(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{t - 2})}{(\sqrt{t})^2 - (\sqrt{t - 2})^2} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{4(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{t-2})}{t - (t - 2)} &=\\[5pt] \dfrac{4(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{t-2})}{2} &=\\[5pt] 2(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{t-2}) \end{align}
